goal: Ensure payload-time source file failures are contained and reported per file across every route while exact-length framing prevents changing files from corrupting adjacent payloads.
recommended_approach: Keep contract v7 and exact-length shard packing, but use one explicit per-path state machine across in-stream, data-plane, resume, and local routes; convert every source preparation/read failure into a skip outcome, make retraction sink-aware, apply consistent handle-based drift checks, and preserve path identity losslessly.
comparison: The change chooses the right core mechanisms and proposes strong acceptance tests and slices, but several incorrect readings of the current implementation leave fatal source paths, ambiguous retraction state, inconsistent drift behavior, and unreliable non-UTF-8 identification.
material_changes: Include resume-file open/read failures and partially emitted resume records in the skip/retraction protocol.
Convert Windows metadata hydration and named-stream failures into per-file outcomes before pipeline-level error propagation.
Replace the granted_headers retraction heuristic with explicit Granted, Active, Completed, and Failed states plus sink-aware cleanup.
Apply the selected size-drift policy after streaming and on the local route, not only before remote record announcement.
Replace U+FFFD inference with lossless or opaque manifest identity for unrepresentable paths.

findings.title: Resume reads remain session-fatal
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:57-58 — the plan calls resume EOF a destination-side read, but crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/resume_diff.rs:1-5 and :66-77 show that ResumeBlockDiff opens the SOURCE file, and :101-119 returns an error on its read or short EOF.
findings.predicted_failure: When a resume-eligible source file becomes unreadable or shrinks after scanning, both carriers propagate the ResumeBlockDiff error and abort the entire session instead of reporting one skipped file.
findings.better_approach: Extend the v7 outcome protocol to resume grants: skip before the first block on open/stat failure, and close an active resume grant as failed without final stamping when a later read fails, leaving or safely discarding the partial according to an explicit sink policy.

findings.title: Windows metadata preparation bypasses containment
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/payload.rs:53-75 — File and TarShard preparation propagate hydrate_payload_header errors with ?, while crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/pipeline.rs:472-475 turns any preparation error into a pipeline failure; this contradicts docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:59-61.
findings.predicted_failure: On Windows, disappearance, access failure, or named-stream size drift after the scan can fail hydration before the proposed open/skip logic runs, cancelling the whole transfer.
findings.better_approach: Make preparation return per-file success or skip outcomes; hydrate shard members independently, and map ordinary-file, resume-file, and named-stream hydration failures to source-prefixed skip records while reserving pipeline errors for non-file infrastructure failures.

findings.title: The proposed retraction state is not present
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:175-187 — retraction assumes an announced path remains in granted_headers after leaving outstanding, but crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/mod.rs:4354-4367 and crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/data_plane.rs:2007-2011 remove both records when the payload is claimed.
findings.predicted_failure: Implemented literally, a post-body skip is classified as an unneeded-path protocol violation and still aborts; merely retaining grants would instead make late or duplicate skips indistinguishable from valid retractions and could unlink a successfully delivered or pre-existing file.
findings.better_approach: Track each need explicitly as Granted, Active with a record token, Completed, or Failed; accept retraction only for the matching active record on its ordered lane, and let the sink abort that specific write or staged temporary file rather than blindly unlinking by path.

findings.title: Size-drift policy is inconsistent across timing and routes
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:258-274 — streamed files are checked only before announcement and local File payloads deliberately copy current bytes, despite the skip policy stated at :15-21 and :393-398.
findings.predicted_failure: A streamed file that grows after the pre-check, or any changing local non-shard file, can be reported as successfully transferred under manifest metadata even though the selected policy says size drift must be skipped.
findings.better_approach: Recheck the opened handle after the bounded stream and retract on drift, and give the local fast path equivalent opened-handle, bounded-copy, and post-copy validation; otherwise narrow the stated goal and acceptance criteria explicitly.

findings.title: Replacement-character detection cannot establish path identity
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/path_posix.rs:40-43 — path components are converted with to_string_lossy, while docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:319-325 proposes inferring invalid UTF-8 from U+FFFD in the resulting string.
findings.predicted_failure: An invalid-byte filename can alias a legitimate filename containing U+FFFD, causing the source to open or report the wrong path; ordinary NotFound errors on legitimate U+FFFD names can also be mislabeled.
findings.better_approach: Detect unrepresentability before lossy conversion and carry a lossless path or opaque manifest-entry identifier in contract v7, with a separate display string for reporting.
